group_assessment.weighting: Perimeter-local count only: one assigned publication, and it is WWOX-direct. This is deliberately not an author-profile count. The article documents an experimental Drosophila/proteomics/genetics group with human-cell follow-up. External author-identity remapping was not repeated because actor identity is explicitly owned by Plan in this assignment. Group identity supplies no uplift to the scientific verdict.

field_density.note: The exact WWOX-IDH and WWOX-SOD title/abstract intersections each contain one record, making this paper uniquely load-bearing for those named edges. These are topic-density queries, not actor-identity remapping.

multihop.note: All 54 references were enumerated sequentially. No cited paper was opened or treated as read because the operator imposed an exclusive PMID perimeter. The JATS marks reference 52 (PMID 18319262, FHIT) with retraction-forward; the FHIT analogy is therefore held and is not used as WWOX evidence.

corpus_crossquery.query: Where does PMID 21075834 already occur and which current redox/metabolism claims does its complete read touch?
corpus_crossquery.note: Post-reading audit found CORPUS P358, LIT-0358, FT-020, surface_census, CLAIM 009, CLAIM 034 and meta_metabolism. The primary result is counter-directional to a monotonic deficit-to-high-ROS reading and supports only a context-dependent sign.

retraction_check.result: Repository retraction gate on 2026-08-11 returned no retraction, expression of concern or correction for PMID 21075834; the XML declares is-retracted=no. The source's reference 52 separately carries a retraction-forward link and is not used as a load-bearing premise.

flagged.citing_relation: Citation in the Discussion (reference 52, with 53) for FHIT gene transfer raising ROS and FHIT binding ferredoxin reductase and malate dehydrogenase; it supports the argued parallel between FHIT and Wwox in ROS control but supplies no data or method of this paper, and the fly ROS result does not depend on it.

entries.proposition: The proteomic and microarray candidates are functional responses rather than known physical WWOX interactors.
entries.snippet: None of the proteins or RNAs detected in these studies, as altered due to increases or decreases in Wwox, is found among those that have previously been reported as having physical interaction with Wwox
entries.anchor: Results, Biochemical responses to altered Wwox levels, paragraph after Table 1

entries.proposition: A negative viability screen does not exclude a functional interaction outside the rate-limiting survival assay.
entries.snippet: The absence of such an interaction, however, does not necessarily rule out a functional interaction between a candidate and Wwox, but rather suggests that within this assay system any interaction between the two proteins is not a rate-limiting requirement for survival of the animal.
entries.anchor: Results, In vivo functional screen for candidate Wwox interactors

entries.proposition: Lower Wwox enhances and higher Wwox suppresses the Idh knock-down viability phenotype across the reported experiments.
entries.snippet: A trend was observed across all five experimental replicates, where a further decrease in viability was observed when Wwox levels were also decreased in these flies, indicating an enhancement of the CG6439/Idh RNAi phenotype
entries.anchor: Results, Functional interaction of CG6439/isocitrate dehydrogenase with Wwox

entries.proposition: The independent double-mutant experiment did not yield adults homozygous for both Wwox and Idh alleles.
entries.snippet: However, we were unable to obtain adult flies that were homozygous for both Idh/CG6439EY00276 and Wwox1, consistent with the enhanced decrease in viability of da > Idh/CG6439RNAi observed when Wwox levels were also decreased by RNAi
entries.anchor: Results, Functional interaction of CG6439/isocitrate dehydrogenase with Wwox, mutant-allele paragraph

entries.proposition: WWOX and IDH1 transcript abundance are positively correlated across the tested human cancer-cell samples.
entries.snippet: A significant positive correlation was observed between endogenous WWOX and IDH1 mRNA levels
entries.anchor: Results, Correlation between WWOX and IDH1 mRNA levels in human cell lines

entries.proposition: Combining Wwox loss with Sod mutant alleles causes a severe synthetic lifespan phenotype.
entries.snippet: This decreased lifespan phenotype was enhanced when the flies were also homozygous mutant for the Wwox1 mutation as Wwox;Sod double-mutant flies all died within the first 24 h of the assay.
entries.anchor: Results, Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase interacts with Wwox

entries.proposition: SOD1 overexpression increases endogenous WWOX in HEK293 whereas the G37R construct does not show that increase.
entries.snippet: This increase in endogenous WWOX mRNA expression was not observed when a G37R mutant form of SOD1 that is associated with ALS
entries.anchor: Results, Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase interacts with Wwox, final paragraph

entries.proposition: Wwox overexpression and loss shift the indirect ROS assay in reciprocal directions.
entries.snippet: In two independent lines of Wwox over-expressing larvae, the percentage of cells with ROS levels above an arbitrary threshold was found to be higher than for control larvae, while Wwox mutants had consistently lower levels of ROS compared with their control larvae
entries.anchor: Results, Wwox affects endogenous levels of ROS

entries.proposition: The ROS readout is indirect CM-H2DCFDA fluorescence measured repeatedly by FACS.
entries.snippet: Intracellular ROS was determined using 5-(and-6)-chloromethyl-2′,7′-dichlorodihydorfluorescein diacetate (CM-H2DCFDA, Molecular Probes), a non-fluorescent dye, which upon deacetylation by cellular esterases and oxidation by ROS becomes fluorescent.
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods, Reactive oxygen species measurements

entries.snippet: The DIGE image contains 28 circled spot labels; spots 19 and 20 are both labelled Sod near the lower-left region.

entries.proposition: Wwox loss alone has no phenotype in the fly, which is why the screen modifies a candidate-RNAi phenotype instead.
entries.snippet: We have previously determined that the loss of Wwox function has no phenotype (29), thus the strategy for our in vivo RNAi screen was first to identify phenotypes produced by altered levels of any of the candidates on their own
entries.anchor: Results, in vivo functional screen
